title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: the 'equation des lacets' is the loop or hexagon-type relation that the Galois action on the profinite fundamental group of P^1 minus {0,1,infinity} must satisfy. Here it is studied through its image in GL(2) over Z-hat. On the preceding pages Grothendieck works with data alpha_0 = (a b; c d) with det alpha_0 = delta = epsilon_3 in {+1,-1}, and f = (r s; t u) with det f = 1. He also uses the fixed matrices rho (order 3), sigma_infinity (order 4) and l_0 = (1 2; 0 1), a parameter mu in Z-hat* and gamma = (mu-1)/2. This is the same pair (lambda, m = (lambda-1)/2) that appears in the GT relations of Drinfeld and Ihara. After a page of explicit 2x2 computations he concludes, at (84), that the result is only a rewriting of the matricial loop relation (56)/(57): eps_2 U = D, eps_2 T = C.

On this page he makes a methodological remark. Under a 'false appearance of arithmetic', the computations are really exercises in linear algebra. They are valid over an arbitrary commutative ring A and, he writes, 'sans doute' under much more general and more 'comprehensive' hypotheses. Two kinds of equation are meant:
(i) Commutator equations [alpha_0, rho] = (given), where rho is in GL(2,A) and the unknown alpha_0 is in GL(2,A), possibly with det alpha_0 = delta fixed.
(ii) Simultaneous equations in alpha_0 and f:
(*) [alpha_0, rho] = eps . E_0(mu-1) [f, sigma], cf. (56).
In (ii), rho and sigma in GL(2,A) and a unit eps in A* are given. lambda -> E_0(lambda) is a one-parameter subgroup, for instance E_0(lambda) = (1 -lambda; 0 1) = eps_0^lambda with eps_0 = (1 -1; 0 1). If needed one assumes a normalization sigma f = eps_0.

He asserts that, modulo 'agreeable adjustments', all formulas of the section should extend to this general context, with substantial complements. On the next page he adds that this includes scheme-theoretic statements. The example given is that the scheme of solutions of (*), with f, alpha_0 and mu variable, is a relative scheme, smooth of relative dimension 4. He then declines to develop this and returns to the 'too particular' adelic case: the Proposition with criterion (85), c^2+cd+d^2 = +/-(t^2+u^2) in Z-hat*. That criterion compares the norm forms of Z[omega] and Z[i], which are attached to the order-3 element rho and the order-4 element sigma_infinity. So the page proposes to treat the GL(2) shadow of the loop or GT relations as a moduli problem: a scheme of solutions of commutator equations over Spec A.
errors: No mathematical errors on this page; it is programmatic.
The smoothness and relative dimension 4 claim (next page) is asserted without proof.

Rough heuristic, not a check: unknowns alpha_0 and f give 8 entries, plus mu makes 9, with one constraint det f = 1. The commutator equation lands in a 3-dimensional determinant-one locus (both sides have the same determinant up to eps^2). Naively this gives 9 - 1 - 3 = 5, not 4. Additional constraints such as det alpha_0 = delta fixed, or the normalization sigma f = eps_0, would plausibly bring this to 4. So the claimed dimension depends on normalizations he leaves unspecified.

ideas.what: Recasting the GL(2,Z-hat) image of the loop (GT-type) relations as linear algebra valid over an arbitrary ring A.
ideas.modern_name: Moduli or representation-scheme viewpoint on commutator equations in GL_2; affine scheme of solutions of word equations.
ideas.usually_credited_to: Representation and character varieties: Culler–Shalen, Lubotzky–Magid (1980s). The GL_2 shadow of GT is not standardly treated this way.

ideas.what: Simultaneous equation [alpha_0, rho] = eps E_0(mu-1)[f, sigma], with a one-parameter unipotent subgroup E_0(lambda) = eps_0^lambda.
ideas.modern_name: Matrix shadow of the GT hexagon/pentagon relation with parameter lambda and m = (lambda-1)/2.
ideas.where_published: Possibly related material in La Longue Marche à travers la théorie de Galois (1981, circulated/edited by Malgoire); unsure about this exact form.

ideas.what: Claim (next page) that the solution scheme of (*) is relatively smooth of relative dimension 4.
ideas.modern_name: Smoothness of a representation-type scheme / fibre of a commutator map.

missed.claim: Grothendieck proposes developing the adelic matrix computations attached to the loop relation as general linear algebra over any ring, with 'substantial complements' and scheme-theoretic interpretations (smoothness of the solution scheme). He explicitly declines to write this out.
missed.quote: Modulo des ajustements agréables, toutes les formules du présent § devraient pouvoir se développer dans ce contexte plus général (ainsi que des compléments substantiels) mais je ne sais si je vais expliciter
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: A scheme over Z parametrizing (alpha_0, f, mu) satisfying the GL_2 image of the GT relations would give an algebraic model for the 'linearized' image of GT-hat or Gal(Q-bar/Q) in GL_2(Z-hat). Its Z-hat-points would recover the adelic Proposition (85)–(87). This viewpoint, GT-type relations cut out a smooth scheme of matrices, does not seem to be developed in the GT literature.

missed.claim: The adelic criterion that follows identifies the solvability condition with the equality of norm forms of Z[omega] and Z[i] (c^2+cd+d^2 = +/-(t^2+u^2)). These are attached to the order-3 and order-4 torsion elements. Combined with the 'any ring A' remark, this suggests a norm-form or torus-theoretic description of the solution scheme.
missed.quote: sous une fausse apparence d'arithmétique, on a fait par la bande des gammes d'algèbre linéaire, valables sur des anneaux quelconques
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It links GT-type relations to tori, namely the norm-one tori for Q(i) and Q(sqrt(-3)), inside GL_2. This is a modest but concrete structural observation.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is mostly a methodological remark. It does announce an unpursued programme: treating the GL_2 image of the loop/GT relations as a scheme over arbitrary rings, with a smoothness claim on the following page. That is an interesting unpublished perspective but not a finished result.
transcription_corrections: Line 2: 'donc sous des conditions' should read 'sans doute sous des conditions'. Line 1 ends '...formulables sans' and line 2 begins 'doute sous des conditions beaucoup plus générales'.
'[\alpha_0,\rho] = \{' : the brace is a blank placeholder for a given right-hand side ('= { }'), not part of a formula.
'ou ρ ∈ Gl(2,A) est donné, ainsi que [crossed: etc.] }' : the closing brace closes the placeholder; 'ainsi que' is an insertion above the line.
'Gl' is Grothendieck's notation for GL; the second line reads 'α_0 ∈ Gl(2,A) est l'inconnue (assujettie éventuellement à des conditions du type det α_0 = δ, δ fixé)'.
